text:
emily_support: Customer acct 8421 reports requests pinned to Dedicated (eu-west-1) are being served from Hosted (us-west-2). High p50/p95 latency + unexpected hosted billing. Can SRE look?
emily_support: They say model traffic should stay in eu-west-1 dedicated pool 'ded-8421-eu'. Example user complaint: "sudden 400-800ms extra latency and +$3k hosted token charge this week".
sam_sre: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and any response headers they saw? Also need request id or trace if available.
emily_support: repro below (token redacted) — they set x-region header and had pin in customer's config:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -H 'X-Region: eu-west-1' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers returned on multiple tries: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
x-served-region: us-west-2
x-route-decisions: fallback->hosted_pool:general
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
mike_infra: That x-route-decisions header is the clue. Routing chose hosted fallback. Can you grab routing service logs for req_0a1b2c3d? Also, did they recently hit a capacity scaling event?
emily_support: Attaching log snippet from customer timeline (redacted):
```
[router] req=req_0a1b2c3d policy=dedicated_affinity evaluate: pool=ded-8421-eu tags=["eu-west-1","dedicated"]
[router] req=req_0a1b2c3d pool_capacity=0.0 available=0.0 -> fallback decision to hosted_pool:general reason="available_capacity"
[router] req=req_0a1b2c3d served_by=hosted-node-17 served_region=us-west-2
```
liz_billing: Customer also says invoice INV-8421-2026-03 has hosted usage entries they don't expect. Can ops provide a list of hosted request_ids for acct 8421 between 1768400000-1768460000 so billing can reconcile?
sam_sre: Quick things: 1) Confirm dedicated pool health/metric (GPU OOMs, drain, scale events). 2) Check pool metadata tag matching — a recent change made tag matching strict. If pool had tag `eu-west-1 ` (trailing space) it would not match. 3) As immediate mitigation, we can set a temporary routing override to refuse hosted fallback for account 8421.
mike_infra: I inspected the pool config for ded-8421-eu — its region tag was accidentally written as "eu-west-1 " (trailing space) in infra repo commit 6f7a2. That explains why affinity eval failed. Pushing hotfix to trim tags on read.
```
repo: infra-configs/owners/dedicated_pools.yaml
- id: ded-8421-eu
  tags: ["eu-west-1 ", "dedicated"]
```
deploybot: CI pipeline green for tag-trim hotfix, promoting to canary. Deployed to router-canary at 1768453300.
sam_sre: After canary, please re-run curl repro and confirm x-served-region == eu-west-1 and x-route-decisions shows pool=ded-8421-eu. If confirmed, we should: (a) backfill missed hosted request_ids for billing, (b) patch infra lint to reject trailing spaces, (c) add an alert for pool tag mismatch.
emily_support: Customer on call wants ETA for crediting hosted charges and guarantee no more cross-region serves. Billing/liz, can we hold off until we confirm repro?
liz_billing: Will prepare provisional credit plan once SRE confirms root cause & timeframe. Send the list of hosted request_ids and USD amount estimate.
mike_infra: Canary looks good — test curl now.
emily_support: Ran repro after canary: response now shows:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-served-region: eu-west-1
x-route-decisions: pool=ded-8421-eu
```
emily_support: Customer confirms latency returned to normal.
sam_sre: Closing loop: root cause = infra config whitespace in region tag causing affinity mismatch -> router fell back to hosted when pool capacity reported 0. Fixes: tag-trim hotfix merged, infra lint rule added, billing reconcile requested, add alert for affinity-fallback spike. Assigning owners: mike_infra (fix + lint), liz_billing (reconcile), sam_sre (alerts + rollback plan).
emily_support: Thanks team :thumbsup: I will update the customer and schedule a post-mortem doc.
